In summary, our approach preserves formal certified unlearning guarantees while substantially mitigating utility loss, opening the door to practical and scalable certified unlearning methods. Our findings suggest that current definitions of certified unlearning may be too strict: they enforce indistinguishability in ways that are not always aligned with practical goals, while still not guaranteeing model utility. A promising direction is to revisit these definitions, aiming for frameworks that both formalize “forgetting” more faithfully and better capture utility preservation. Beyond this conceptual aspect, further work includes exploring adaptive block decompositions, scaling to larger and more complex architectures, and narrowing the remaining gap between certified unlearning and retraining.
